title: Playing in a brass band before fourteen
summary: Howard confirms playing triple-tongue solos and travelling to Columbus with a brass band before he was fourteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: It mentioned here--jumping back to Ohio again--that --it said that before you were fourteen, you were playing triple-tongue solos, among other technical feats, and traveled to Columbus, Ohio for a musical appearance.
Yes, yes. Forgot all about that. What did he say the last was?
(laughter) That you had traveled to Columbus, Ohio for a musical appearance. That was before you were fourteen.
I did. Went to Columbus, Ohio-- musical appearance.
What was--was that with the older band you played with, or what group was it with?
No, it was with the band. Brass band.
Oh. Did the brass band have a name?
Huh?
Did the brass band have a name?
No. Didn't have no name. Just--
You were like a Boy Wonder?
(laughter)--Man, playin' all over.
Oh. On the road before he was 14.
(inaudible) now, he started all this.

They got me out there. Soon as I got a chance to get out there and get that horn into my lips. I used to love to play. I do love to play yet. I just don't keep a horn in the hand. Buddy can tell you--he's heard me play, and watched--
He's some player, all right.
Buddy has told me a lot. Buddy--
Pardon?
Buddy has told me a lot about what a fine musician you are. I'm sorry that I never got to hear you.
(inaudible) (laughter) I love to play. My wife listens to me play, all of 'em. When I--don't play no more. I don't think I'm gonna play no more.
Well, you might.
Might. Can't never tell. But I wish that you could see my--hear my people sing and play. That was my--you know--my relatives, sing and play.
